title: Close out an access panel with retainer bars
instruction: Seat the grey panel flush in its pocket, then lay each orange retainer bar flat across the panel edge into its rib slot, at least 20 mm onto the panel.
context: Access-panel close-out is routine aircraft and spacecraft integration work (aircraft structure and systems assemblers, O*NET 51-2011): the cover goes into its recess flush, then retainers are set across the joint. Unlike a part dropped into a pocket, each retainer bridges the panel and the frame, so its seat exists only once the panel is flush. A bar laid first tips about 23 degrees into the empty pocket and must be lifted out again, and a panel left proud tilts the bar past 3 degrees. 1 g tabletop analogue; a real panel is held by quarter-turn or captive fasteners under spring preload, which this task does not reproduce. No microgravity is claimed.
setup: Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and y = -0.305 (right). The pocket centre F is (0.250, 0.000), on the midline. Loose, rigid, matte: the panel, a dark grey (sRGB 0.20, 0.20, 0.22) block 160 x 80 x 16 mm, 120 g (printed PLA), lying flat centred at (0.220, 0.330) with its long axis along y; two retainer bars, orange (sRGB 0.95, 0.55, 0.10) blocks 60 x 16 x 16 mm, 10 g each (printed PLA), lying along x in their keyways on the frame plates, bar_plus centred at (0.250, 0.113) and bar_minus at (0.250, -0.113), bottoms 16 mm above the table. Fixed, light grey (sRGB 0.80, 0.80, 0.82), matte, 18 blocks in all, forming one frame: a pocket ring 5 mm tall standing on the table, two walls 186 x 10 x 5 mm centred at (0.250, +0.048) and (0.250, -0.048) and two walls 10 x 86 x 5 mm centred at (0.162, 0.000) and (0.338, 0.000), giving an open pocket 166 x 86 mm whose floor is the table (3 mm of clearance per side around the panel, at most about 2 degrees of yaw); two frame plates 220 x 80 x 16 mm centred at (0.250, +0.093) and (0.250, -0.093), spanning 53 to 133 mm either side of the midline against the ring's outer faces, their tops 16 mm above the table and flush with a seated panel's top; on each plate, a keyway of four ribs 10 x 4 x 10 mm (x, y, z) centred at x 0.223 and 0.277 and y 0.101 and 0.125 (mirrored for the right plate), their inner faces 20 mm apart (2 mm either side of the stowed bar), flanking the last 8 mm at each end of the bar, 2 mm from its sides, with the bar's end faces open; on each plate, a slot of two ribs 4 x 10 x 10 mm centred at x 0.237 and 0.263 and y 0.071 (mirrored), their inner faces 22 mm apart (3 mm either side of a set bar), spanning 66 to 76 mm from the midline, tops 26 mm above the table, with nothing across either end of the slot. Nominal end state: the panel centred on F with its long axis along x, flat on the table inside the ring, top flush with the plates; each bar along y centred at (0.250, +0.046) or (0.250, -0.046), spanning 16 to 76 mm from the midline: 24 mm on the panel, 13 mm across the 3 mm gap and the ring wall (whose top is 11 mm below the bar), 23 mm on the plate, its outer 10 mm between the slot ribs and its outer end in line with their outer faces. With top-down grips the panel and bar_plus are within the left arm's reach and bar_minus within the right arm's; F is 0.25 m out on the midline, within both. To build it: print the ring and both plates with their ribs as one open-floored PLA frame about 220 x 266 mm, tape it to the table with its outline marked, and print the panel and bars to the stated sizes and masses. If the print bed is under 266 mm, print the frame as two halves split on the midline (each about 220 x 133 mm) and tape both to the marked outline.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arms have withdrawn and nothing moves (in simulation: at rest, speed under 10 mm/s and spin under 0.5 rad/s), from a top photo, a straightedge, a steel rule and a phone level. Panel seated (P): at rest with its centre within 4 mm of F in x and y, long axis within 3 degrees of x either way round, all four bottom corners within 2 mm of the table and all four top corners within 2 mm of the plate tops (16 mm up), so a panel cocked on a ring wall, proud, outside the pocket or held above it fails. A bar is set in a slot when it rests with its long axis within 10 degrees of y either way round, a face within 3 degrees of flat, its lowest corner within 2 mm of the plate tops, its centre within 4 mm of the slot's centre line (x = 0.250) across the slot, its outer end (the end away from the midline) within 4 mm of the ribs' outer faces (76 mm from the midline) along the slot, and its inner end at least 20 mm inside the panel's edge, measured across the panel from where the panel actually lies. Either bar may fill either slot and each slot counts once. Score: 0 without P, whatever the bars do; P alone 0.4; P and one slot filled 0.7; P and both slots filled 1.0. Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. Order: without a seated panel, a bar laid in a slot has its centre 7 mm past the plate edge and tips about 23 degrees into the empty pocket, its inner end on the table; on a panel resting 5 mm proud on the ring it tilts about 8 degrees, pivoting on the panel edge; both fail the 3 degree test. A bar on the panel outside a slot, across the joint along x, on the rib tops, stacked on the other bar, on the table, held above its slot (lowest corner more than 2 mm above the plate tops) or moving earns nothing for that slot. Photo check: the panel inside the ring with no step to a straightedge laid across both plates; each bar level and in its slot between the two ribs, its outer end within 4 mm of a straightedge laid across the two ribs' outer faces (76 mm from the midline), and a rule from its inner end to the panel edge reads at least 20 mm. The frame is fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which the frame moved more than 2 mm from its taped outline scores 0. In simulation the scorer cannot see the grippers, so a panel or bar still gripped but motionless at the end is not distinguished; on the real rig the photo is taken after the arms park.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lift the panel out and lay it flat on its start mark, long axis along y; lay each bar back in its keyway along x. The frame does not move; check it against its taped outline.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and matte colours; the ring, plates and ribs are fixed colliders standing in for one printed frame. A real quarter-turn or captive fastener turns in place under spring preload; here each loose bar is set across the joint and holds the panel by its weight only. The 3 mm panel clearance is looser than a flight panel's. Earth gravity on a bench, where this job is done.
